caption: The video captures a black-rimmed analog wall clock lying face-up on cracked asphalt, its dial reading about 2:35 while a pale cord trails from its base. A small water-filled depression sits just beyond it and a broad dark damp patch spreads across the right half of the pavement, edged by grass at the top. The clock casing, puddle, damp patch and surface cracks hold fixed positions throughout, with no camera movement. The hour and minute hands stay essentially stationary, aimed between two and three and at the seven. The only visible motion is the thin second hand with a red tail, which sweeps steadily clockwise across the dial. Already moving at the first frame, it advances continuously from the eight position over the top toward the five, still in motion at the last.
